thread.title: Texas Instruments: Chip Slowdown or Just High Expectations?

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Texas Instruments: Chip Slowdown or Just High Expectations?
text:
Shares of analog chip giant Texas Instruments ( TXN ) are down $6.14, or 5%, at $113.75, continuing last night’s after-hours decline , after the company forecast results this quarter just a little bit above consensus, which has prompted a debate over whether the business is slowing down.
In addition, the company’s inventory rose during the quarter, which many are pointing to today as a concern.
A minor technicality in the report last quarter’s numbers, Q4, was that profit was depressed by an unexpected charge pertaining to adjustments for the new tax regulations in the U.S. T.I. said its tax rate is set to go much lower, however, next year.
Shares of fellow analog chip maker Analog Devices ( ADI ) are off by 33 cents at $96.14.
The negative case is made by, among others, SunTrust Robinson Humphrey ’s William Stein , who reiterates a Hold rating, writing that “ something’s not quite right. "
"TXN is an outstanding operator and delivered ~inline results & guide,” he writes. "Still, relative to conservative guidance, strong GDP, and effervescent semi managements, it feels like a miss to us."
To Stein, there’s a structural issue holding back semi sales here:
On 12/1/17 we revised our view on semis from constructive to balanced, and highlighted that the most significant fundamental risk to semis today is that shortages in complementary passive & discrete components could limit semi industry sales growth later this year. While we may be expressing confirmation bias, and TXN's results may be more isolated to comms infra weakness, we believe the results (weaker than buyside expectations combined with an inventory expansion) fit our narrative better. That is: shortages in passives/discretes have led to bloated semi inventories at customers that is leading to slower orders on semis. We continue to advocate an equal-weighting in semis as these risks are balanced by what we believe is still strong demand. Our top long ideas in this fading-growth part of the cycle are structural growers NVDA and MPWR. Other buy-rated names are MSCC, AVGO, and ADI.
Other bears see some slowing, but nothing dramatic.
Raymond James ’s Chris Caso , reiterating a Market Perform rating, writes that Apple ’s (AAPL) iPhone may be causing a slowing of demand, but also T.I.’s 24 times P/E multiple is higher and probably played a role, he thinks:
We suspect that both Communications equipment and iPhone served to constrain upside from what we believe is continuing strength in Auto and Industrial. We expect such commentary to represent the dominant theme as we proceed through semi earnings. Nonetheless, as investors have oscillated between fears of conditions being too strong (causing overheating), or too weak, TXN’s results appear to signal neither. We think the recent run and premium valuation of TXN stock likely required more upside from the quarter to support the current valuation, however the results don’t meaningfully change our thesis on the broader group.
The bulls see little here to be worried about.
John Pitzer of Credit Suisse , who has an Outperform rating on the stock, titles his note this morning “ Not good enough ."
"With a stock up 15% YTD, at all-time highs, and expectations for a beat/raise, an essentially in-line C4Q and a modest C1Q EPS miss adj. for tax will not be good enough,” he observes.
He concedes there’s risk of a slowdown, though he’s not too worried at this point:
TXN highlighted Comms weakness and we suspect AAPL was less of a tailwind than expected. TXN guided C1Q seasonal, the 1st guide not below seasonal in 4 Qs – giving some confidence in demand […] We continue to have a LT positive bias on the sector – albeit NT cyclical noise caused by decelerating growth is a risk.
Hans Mosesmann of Rosenblatt Securities , who has a Buy rating on the shares, and a $135 price target, thinks the outlook is just fine, and like Pitzer he acknowledges a "merely an in-line quarter and guide” is spooking "investors used to beat-and-raises."
"The notion that TI can grow the top line at 10% plus levels organically, as was the case in 2017, is simply untenable. However, 5-7% growth is we think a sweet spot for TI in terms of sales growth."
Mosesmann thinks that the worries about inventories are a bit too much:
Inventories at 134 days, up 8 days y/y, were a topic of some concern on the earnings call even though management indicated they were within normal rang- es, were as expected, and with no change lead-times or inventory in the chan- nel at 4 weeks. Management characterized inventory decisions, in the current case a tad more than last year, as a tactical call to ensure customers a high level of service and that these slightly higher inventories are of higher quality analog/embedded (not high volume more commodity analog). We view the top- ic with mild curiosity mostly on how the street may choose to react to the TI business move here and not on some signal of the end of a cycle or execution issues.
Stacy Rasgon with Bernstein reiterates an Outperform rating, and raises his price target to $125 from $120, writing that the results “were quite solid,” and that the sell off can be attributed "to general fears of peaking sector fundamentals (with in-line results rather than a beat) as well as the extremely strong recent performance in the shares (up almost 60% over the last year and almost 15% since the start of 2018)."
Still, "structural fundamentals remain strong” and "Investors who have been looking for a better entry point may thus receive one."
